jobs.occupation: Logistics Manager to Beyond Gravity Linköping
jobs.description:
🚀 Challenge the Impossible​ ​
 
About Beyond Gravity
 
Beyond Gravity, headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland, is the first space company to combine a startup mindset, agility, speed and innovation with decades of experience and proven quality. Approximately 1800 employees at 12 locations in six countries (Switzerland, Sweden, Austria, USA, Finland and Portugal) develop and manufacture products for satellites and launch vehicles with the goal of advancing humankind and enabling the exploration of the world and beyond. Beyond Gravity is the preferred supplier of structures for all types of launch vehicles and a leading provider of selected satellite products and constellation solutions in the New Space sector. In 2024, the company generated a revenue of around CHF 359 million. More information at: www.beyondgravity.com
 
Your crew

Beyond Gravity is in a strong growth and transformation phase. At our Linköping site, one of Beyond Gravity's key manufacturing operations, we are moving from a project-oriented way of working to a scalable and volume-oriented delivery model, with high demands for precision, pace and quality.
 
The Supply Chain function consists of logistics, planning and procurement, where the logistics function is currently in a development and transformation phase with a need for clearer structure, processes and control.
 
In this role, you report to the Senior Manager Supply Chain and have personnel responsibility for approximately 18 employees working across warehouse and logistics operations.

Your mission
 
The role as Logistics Manager in Linköping is a central and critical position within the Supply Chain function. Here you will have the opportunity to lead and develop the logistics function in an environment characterized by high technical complexity, an international environment and a clear focus on transformation. The assignment involves creating structure, stability and long-term sustainable ways of working in an environment where the pace is high and where logistics is crucial to production.
 
You will combine strategic development work with close operational leadership. The role initially requires you to be hands-on in the development of improved processes, efficient material flows and high delivery reliability. The role as Logistics Manager is therefore a key role in succeeding with the work to improve logistics flows. This challenge is suitable for you who thrive in transformation environments and are motivated by building, improving and developing operations together with your team.
 
Responsibilities:
Lead and develop the logistics and warehouse team in the daily operation
Develop and implement logistics strategy, processes and guidelines
Act as process owner for all logistics processes and related documentation
Responsible for the daily management of logistics personnel and ensuring an organizationally efficient structure adapted to the needs of the business
Responsible for a correctly managed warehouse and its processes, including audit-safe inventory, as well as warehouse analyses
Lead the team within the cost center budget, including necessary asset and investment planning
Develop and establish key performance indicators to measure and manage all logistics processes
Drive continuous process optimization within the area of responsibility

Your story
 
We are looking for you who are a confident, experienced and present leader with the ability to create structure and stability in a complex operation. You thrive in environments where change is a natural part of everyday work and have a solution-oriented approach with the ability to combine operational action with long-term improvement work.
 
You are a person who is motivated by developing both people and processes and who creates engagement through clarity, collaboration and a coaching leadership style. The role requires a high level of presence in the operation, good prioritization skills and a good ability to handle a high pace.
 
Must-haves:
Post-secondary education in logistics or a similar field – or equivalent experience
Solid background and understanding of logistics within manufacturing industry, as well as experience of cross-functional collaboration between logistics, production, planning and procurement
Solid formal management experience with experience in developing teams
Experience in driving and developing transformation and improvement work within logistics
Experience of warehouse responsibility and material management
Experience in creating structure, processes and ways of working in operations with a high pace and change
Fluent knowledge of Swedish and English, spoken and written
Good system knowledge, preferably SAP, as well as good experience working in a data-driven and process-oriented manner

 
Why Beyond Gravity
 
To work in a growing high technology company with career opportunities within the site or internationally.
You will be a part of an engaged team with the ambition to innovate space!
We offer a hybrid work situation, high flexibility and autonomy, and a great team to develop and have fun with!

 
🌌Are you ready for lift-off?​
 
Our core values - Passionate, Together, and Curious - transform challenges into opportunities. Embark on a journey to transcend the ordinary with us. We‘re actively reviewing candidates and will promptly select the ideal fit for our team.​
 
For questions regarding the position, please contact: ​Joakim Käll | joakim.kaell@beyondgravity.com 
​
For questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact: ​Breno Silva | breno.silva@beyondgravity.com 
​
Beyond Gravity is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We welcome and encourage applications from all qualified individuals, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, gender, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other legally protected categories.​
​
Applications by e-mail cannot be considered. We do not accept dossiers from recruitment agencies for this position.

Do you want to furnish the future with innovative products?
With us, you can feel at home in your work while sharing that feeling with millions of people around the world. We encourage you to speak up for yourself and others, creating an environment where everyone feels welcome. We invite you to open new doors, discover new tech possibilities, embrace mistakes, and grow from them. As our Team Manager, you'll have many opportunities to try things you've never done before.
IKEA Supply is responsible for the supply chain strategy, supply planning and logistics services that ensure IKEA products are available to customers around the world in a cost efficient, sustainable way. Every day, we strive to make our supply chain smarter, faster and more resilient.
You will belong to the Supply Data & Analytics team, reporting to the Data & Analytics Manager. We are enabling data democratisation through scalable self-service capabilities and AI enablement, while ensuring high quality, timely and cost efficient data products that support IKEA Supply in making more informed and effective business decisions.
Job Description
As Team Manager you will lead our Data Scientist competence hub, a home for people who share a craft, and in the future the role may extend to include other roles too. Our Data & Analytics team works in a product operating model: cross-functional data product teams, guided by product leaders, own and continuously improve data products that create lasting value for IKEA Supply. The product teams own what is built and why; you own the people and the craft, making sure your team members are motivated, growing and set up to do great work in those teams. Your most important job is to be a great manager. You will also be a trusted technical guide for the team on methods, quality and good practice, and collaborate closely with product owners, Data & Digital Product Leaders and stakeholders across IKEA Supply.
In this role, your typical week can look something like this:
Leading, coaching and developing your team members through regular one-to-ones, feedback, career conversations and clear expectations, creating a safe and inclusive team culture.
Taking care of recruitment, onboarding, competence development and succession planning for your competence hub.
Making sure your Data Scientists are well placed in cross-functional data product teams, partnering with product owners on priorities and capacity, and removing blockers so the team can deliver value continuously.
Providing technical leadership for the Data Scientists, supporting sound modelling, statistics, machine learning and experimentation practices, and making sure quality is built into every deliverable.
Making sure insights and conclusions from data science are clear, trusted and easily available to business stakeholders, and that statistical and machine learning concepts are explained to non-technical audiences.
Collaborating with data engineers, analysts, architects and peers to ensure consistent methodologies, tools and ways of working across Supply Data & Analytics and the wider IKEA data community.
Supporting responsible use of AI and AI assisted tools in data science work, and keeping up to date with technology trends and business needs.
Contributing to planning and budgeting by providing input on resources, development and investment needs.

Qualifications
What we'd like you to bring to the table
The role as a Team Manager is a good match if you bring:
Direct or indirect people management experience: leading people to perform and deliver, developing competence, recruiting and planning succession. Strong people skills, empathy and a coaching mindset are what matter most.
A genuine passion for building inclusive, high-trust teams where people feel safe to grow, make mistakes and learn from them.
Strong technical background in data science or similar, with experience developing data driven products for real-life business problems, and the ability to guide Data Scientists on approach and quality.
Experience in understanding business needs and turning them into data products that deliver measurable value, in close collaboration with product leaders.
The ability to clearly communicate statistical and machine learning concepts to non-technical audiences and to build strong relationships with stakeholders and product owners.
Experience working in a product operating model and in an agile set-up, with an understanding of data product principles such as iterative delivery, ownership and continuous improvement.
A bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science or a related quantitative field; an advanced degree is preferred.

It's a plus if you also have:
Experience leading data science teams in a large enterprise or complex matrixed organisation, ideally within supply chain, logistics or manufacturing.
Experience leading teams within a product operating model, partnering with Data & Digital Product Leaders or equivalent.
Experience introducing common ways of working, tools and competence in the business.
Experience with budgeting and resource planning.
Experience applying generative AI or agent based workflows in data science.
Experience leading or growing several different roles or competence areas within data and analytics.

Additional information
This team is located in Malmö, Sweden. We regret that we are unable to handle applications made by e-mail. We only handle applications in English. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible, but no later than 15th Dec. 2026. Ensure that you include your CV and Motivation Letter.
At IKEA, we are looking for people who believe everyone deserves a seat at the table. You're welcome no matter where you come from, what you believe and what you look like. We don't even care how you have furnished your home. We're interested in you simply because you're you. Even if your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. We believe that people's different perspectives, backgrounds and personalities make us better at understanding our customers' dreams and needs. If you have a special need that requires accommodation in the recruitment process, just let us know.
We are looking forward to hearing from you soon!

Join Truecaller – The place where innovation meets impact!
Truecaller's mission is to build trust in communication by making it safer, smarter, and more efficient. Born in Sweden, trusted by the world, and here’s why we stand out:
We are trusted by over 500 million active users every month across 190+ countries
We identify over 15 billion calls daily, helping users avoid spam and scams
We are powered by a team of 400+ employees from 45+ nationalities

We always look for people who take initiative, own their work, and keep raising the bar. An entrepreneurial mindset matters here, especially when it turns bold ideas into real actions. We stay collaborative and focused, always searching for smarter paths forward. If you want to make an impact and grow with a team that inspires millions, you’ll fit right in.
The role
You will lead the Decisioning squad as its most senior data scientist: data scientists, ML engineers, and backend engineers across Stockholm and India. This is a hands-on leadership role. You will still write models, run the offline evaluations, and read the experiment results yourself.
What you'll do:
Own the modelling roadmap for decisioning - conversion prediction, ranking, campaign selection and bidding - and agree it with product and engineering.
Design, build and run production models end to end, from problem framing and features through offline evaluation, A/B tests and monitoring.
Evolve the contextual bandit from choosing which campaign to show to setting a per-request bid, with exploration, off-policy evaluation and safe rollout built in.
Keep model scores honest: calibration per campaign and placement, and a clear link between offline metrics and the revenue and conversions advertisers actually see.
Set the bar for experimentation in the squad: every model change ships with a holdout, an agreed success metric and a clear ship or kill rule.
Lead the squad: set the technical direction, review designs and code, run the prioritisation, and grow the data scientists, engineers and interns around you. You are accountable for what the squad ships, not only for your own work.
Write the RFCs and decision records the group works from, and present results and trade-offs to product, commercial and executive leadership.
Work with backend and data engineering on serving latency, feature pipelines and data quality, so models run reliably at very high throughput.
Raise the data science practice across Revenue Intelligence and the wider discipline through reviews, shared methods and mentoring.

What you bring in:
7+ years in data science or applied machine learning, including several years owning models in production that real revenue depends on.
Depth in ranking, recommendation or conversion prediction at scale - multi-task learning, deep learning and gradient-boosted models, and calibration.
Hands-on experience with online learning or decision systems, such as contextual bandits, exploration strategies and off-policy evaluation.
Strong experimentation skills: A/B test design, power, causal reasoning, and telling a real lift from noise.
Expert Python and SQL, with a modern deep learning framework (TensorFlow/Keras or PyTorch) and a cloud warehouse at real scale. We run on GCP and BigQuery; equivalent depth on another stack transfers.
Technical leadership of a team: setting direction, reviewing other people's work, and raising the quality of the people around you.
Strong written English. You will write the RFCs, evaluation reports and design docs, and they will be read by people who were not in the room.
Comfort operating across Sweden and India time zones.

It will be great if you also have:
Ad tech experience - real-time bidding, auctions, pacing, attribution or campaign delivery.
Experience with the India digital advertising market and performance advertisers.
An MSc or PhD in computer science, statistics, mathematics or a related field.
Experience taking models to low-latency serving, and the MLOps around it: model registries, monitoring and automated retraining.
Exposure to privacy-constrained modelling, such as GDPR and India's DPDP Act.
Experience applying LLMs to modelling or analysis work.

What we offer: 
We support growth through learning resources, leadership programs, mentoring, and real hands-on work. People can move between teams and projects to build new skills and keep things interesting. We offer clear internal mobility and a transparent path for progression, with leaders who stay involved and provide guidance throughout the year. In addition, you will benefit from: 
A comprehensive compensation package: We offer a competitive salary, 30 days of paid vacation, private health insurance, parental leave top-up, pension, and wellness contributions.
Modern tools to do your best work: Choose your preferred computer and phone within our budget, so you can work comfortably and efficiently.
A people-focused office culture: We value in-person collaboration and follow an office-first model, with some flexibility. Our offices offer a vibrant environment with opportunities to learn, connect, and recharge, from breakfast, lunch, and well-stocked snack stations and quiet spaces to team activities such as movie nights, tech meetups, and cultural events. There's something for everyone.
Truecaller’s “Lab Days” offer a space for imagination: 5 times per year for 3 days, where everyone steps away from their normal tasks to explore new, bold ideas and build things they’ve always wanted to. It’s a space where curiosity leads the way, and prototypes take shape. Some concepts even make it into production, and a few have grown into real features used by millions today. Lab Days allow you to be creative, learn fast, and help shape Truecaller's future.

Come as you are:
Truecaller is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We believe that a wide range of backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences strengthens our products and our culture. No matter where you're from, what language you speak, or how you identify, we value what makes you unique and would love to get to know you.

Why RLB? 
We value your skills, talents and unique perspectives – we think they are priceless.  
Bring them to RLB and you'll be empowered to shape our future and your career in new and meaningful ways. 
We'll give you opportunities to work on some of the most ambitious and exciting projects currently being designed and developed in the built environment sector. 
You'll continue to learn and advance as everyone who works for us is provided with a tailored training programme. Our mentoring and reverse mentoring schemes will enable you to share your expertise while gaining fresh insights. 
What makes RLB unique is our inclusive culture. As an independent, employee-owned business, teamwork and collaboration lies at the heart of everything we do. Hybrid and flexible working arrangements and family-friendly policies are just some of the ways we invest in employee wellbeing. 
Join us and you will thrive personally as well as professionally. 
 
Role Overview:
The OFCI Project Manager will manage the procurement of critical mechanical and electrical plant and equipment for large-scale construction projects. This role ensures the timely, on-budget delivery of projects that meet client expectations and stakeholder satisfaction. The OFCI Project Manager will oversee the design, fabrication, inspection, approval, installation, commissioning, and handover of critical plant and equipment on behalf of the client and the project team.
The ideal candidate will have a mechanical or electrical background and will be responsible for monitoring day-to-day activities in the field. This includes managing and coordinating information flow, as well as reporting and tracking issues related to progress, quality, and safety. The role will also require client-facing communication with proven organizational and interpersonal skills.
Role Responsibilities:
Assist in the delivery of a wide range of projects.
Engage with vendors to identify project risks and ensure these risks are assessed and managed throughout the design, fabrication, and installation stages.
Review technical submissions from vendors and/or contractors to ensure compliance with the client's specifications.
Prepare for and facilitate meetings, ensuring all minutes are recorded.
Attend meetings, monitor progress, and escalate any issues that may arise.
Implement project procedures and ensure they are consistently followed.
Assist with the change management process.
Support the implementation of key project processes to ensure successful project delivery, and monitor these processes while reporting and making recommendations to the client team.
Conduct regular site walks to promote safety and monitor progress; report and track corrective actions through to completion.
Regularly inspect the site, obtain progress and quality reports, and ensure non-conforming work is addressed.
Assist in the review and assessment of proposed variations and any delays to project progress.
Support the development of the handover plan, track documentation preparation, and coordinate snagging activities with the client, consultant, and contractor teams.
Work closely with the client's vendors to ensure timely delivery and installation of critical project equipment. This includes equipment like Generators, MV Switchgear, LV Switchgear, BAS, EPMS, AHUs, UPS, etc.
Align the Vendor Equipment Schedule with the overall project timeline in collaboration with the Lead Project Manager and client.
Engage with vendors early in the manufacturing process and align factory witness tests with project milestones.
Work with the appointed General Contractor (GC) and specialist subcontractors to ensure correct work methods and installation requirements are followed. Ensure that method statements are approved in advance of installation.
Manage paperwork and sign-offs associated with vendor equipment installation.
Advise the client's design team on vendor equipment-related elements, where applicable.
At the start of your involvement, review deliverables and role requirements with the Lead Project Manager and client program lead to ensure all client-specific needs are addressed.
Attend Factory Witness Testing (FWT) and Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) and visit off-site manufacturing plants to ensure quality control measures are followed and to inspect equipment prior to shipping.

Candidate Profile
Experience
Previous experience in Data Centre facility maintenance, operation, and/or commissioning.
A Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related field is beneficial.
Proficiency with various computer software applications, including MS Office (Excel, Outlook, Project, Word), is required. Experience with online document management applications (e.g., Procore, Bluebeam) is a strong plus.
Strong communication and organizational skills.
Experience in Manufacturing QA/QC.
Fluent in English (both verbal and written communication).

RLB Employee Benefits
Our culture is built around enabling you to fulfil your potential, so you can look forward to benefits that include:
Hybrid Working - Working patterns to support your work-life balance. 
Well-Rewarded - A competitive salary and generous holiday entitlement. As well as the opportunity to purchase up to five extra days.
Personal Development - A continuous learning and development programme, including established APC and in-house mentoring schemes.
Additional Benefits - We offer a wide range of benefits including professional membership subscriptions.
Exceptional Exposure - You'll have the opportunity to work on diverse projects across different sectors and regions.
Social Responsibility - We hold team and social events as well as charity fundraising and volunteering activities.

Our Diversity & Inclusion Promise
We believe in building a diverse and inclusive environment where each person can be themselves, feel valued for their contribution and be challenged and supported to reach their full potential. We have a responsibility to support the communities in which we live and work, and that our workforce should reflect these communities and our clients. Our talent strategy should enable us to overcome bias in the construction industry by recruiting, retaining, developing, and promoting a diverse and inclusive workforce. Find out more here: Diversity & Inclusion - RLB | Europe 
If you require any reasonable adjustments to support you during any stage of the application or interview process, please contact our recruitment team at: recruitment@uk.rlb.com

About the role
Imagine HR where efficient, trusted processes and AI go hand in hand: smooth onboarding, people data everyone can trust, and reliable AI answers to everyday questions about how we work. As our AI-Driven HR Operations Specialist, you make that happen. You design, document, and automate our core HR processes, and you put AI to work wherever it does the job better, so managers and employees across Tacton spend less time on admin and more time on what matters. This is the role for someone who thinks in processes, rules, and data flows, gets a real buzz from what AI can do, and wants to turn that into everyday impact.
You'll report directly to Eva Lessing, our CHRO, and team up with the HR team, our AI Automation Specialist, IT, and Security and Compliance to bring your ideas to life.
What you will do
• Build the HR automation and AI roadmap, prioritizing by business value, process readiness, data sensitivity, and effort, and choosing between automation, AI, or leaving a process as it is. Then build and run the solutions that make HR work smarter for everyone at Tacton.
• Run, document and continuously improve our core HR processes: onboarding and offboarding, goal setting, performance review, and our engagement survey.
• Own our HRIS (Workday) and Performance system (Leapsome), and set up, maintain, and reconfigure integrations with other systems such as our ATS (Teamtailor), LMS (Docebo), and Microsoft Entra ID.
• Set up dashboards and self-service reporting so managers and HR get reliable people data whenever they need it.
• Make sure every solution meets our security and privacy requirements, including ISO 27001 and SOC 2.
• Measure results in time saved, error rates, and adoption, and enable HR colleagues and managers so the changes stick.
What we are looking for
• 5+ years in HR, ideally in HR operations, HR systems, or HR technology, with hands-on experience designing and automating HR processes and a solid understanding of people data.
• A genuine curiosity and passion for what AI can do, backed by hands-on experience with AI tools such as Claude (our main AI tool at Tacton), ChatGPT, or Microsoft Copilot, including AI and automation solutions you have built and maintained, such as workflows and assistants, with measurable results.
• Strong skills in documenting processes so others can follow them.
• A self-driven way of working, comfort with ambiguity, and a collaborative style. You bring HR, IT, Security, and Compliance colleagues along and can explain trade-offs to senior stakeholders.
• Good judgment with confidential employee data.
• Fluent English. Swedish and Workday experience are a plus.
Your first six months
• Map how our HR processes and integrations work today.
• Agree a roadmap with priorities and baseline measures.
• Get at least two improvements live and measured.
• Introduce a documentation standard that the HR team uses.
Why join us
• You build it from the ground up. This is a brand-new role with no playbook to inherit. The processes, standards, and AI solutions you create become how HR works at Tacton.
• Your expertise matters from day one. Our HR team already uses AI and is eager to do more, but we need an expert to lead the way. You will raise the bar for all of us, and because the need is big, your work will be seen and truly appreciated.
• Your impact reaches the whole company. Every process you simplify saves time and increases quality for employees and managers in every country we operate in.
• You have room to move fast. You report to our CHRO, who sees her job as removing obstacles for you. You join an engaged HR team of six in Stockholm, Chicago, and Karlsruhe that loves trying new things.
• You grow with a company on the move. Tacton develops every day and is expanding from a single product into a full platform, so the role grows as you grow.
What to expect during the recruitment process
• Screening call with Global Talent Acquisition Partner
• First interview with our hiring manager
• Personality and logical ability test
• Second interview and peer meeting, which will include a case
• Interview with senior management
• Reference checks
• Background checks
What we offer
At Tacton, you'll develop your career in an organization that values teamwork and promotes individual growth. We offer a global and open environment, working with the latest technology to solve important and complex problems in the manufacturing industry.
• Flexible hybrid setup: 3 days a week in the office.
• 33 days of paid time off: 30 vacation days plus 3 extra to make sure you get the rest you deserve.
• Premium occupational pension: Our pension plan goes beyond ITP1, with higher employer contributions depending on your age and salary level.
• Generous wellness allowance: 5,000 SEK annually to support your health and wellbeing.
• Private healthcare insurance: Skip the waiting lines and get quick access to private medical care, including specialist consultations and treatments.
• Parental leave top-up: We top up your parental leave, so you receive up to 90% of your base salary for up to 6 months, helping you focus on your family without financial stress.
• Weekly treats: Fika one week, breakfast the next, because good food brings people together.

Promise what you can build. Build what you promised. For 26 years, Tacton has helped manufacturers of complex products around the world do exactly that. Now we’re taking configuration intelligence further than ever. Through Tacton’s Connected Suite, every configuration flows on one digital thread from product definition to the factory floor, and AI agents can promise only what can actually be built. Learn more at www.tacton.com.

Boliden is a high-tech metals company with its own mines and smelters that works long-term to guarantee society's access to base and precious metals. For a century, our work has been part of the value chains that have shaped modern society. At Boliden, we know that the metals we mine and make available will continue to play a crucial role in the future – what matters is how we produce them. Become a part of us and drive change for generations to come. 
 
Your opportunity
Technology is transforming the metals industry, creating new opportunities to improve safety, sustainability, productivity, and business performance. 
As Head of IT Smelters, you will play a key role in shaping the digital future of Boliden's Smelter operations. In this highly visible leadership position, you will drive the technology strategy, lead business-critical transformation initiatives, and ensure that digital solutions create lasting value across one of Europe's leading metals companies. 
If you are passionate about combining business leadership with technology and want to make a real impact, this is an opportunity to influence the future of an industry essential to modern society.
We look forward to receiving your application!
 
Who you will work with
As a member of the IT Leadership Team, reporting to the CIO, you will play a key role in shaping Boliden's technology agenda and contributing to strategic decision-making across the organization. You will lead a team of seven IT managers and specialists while partnering closely with Smelter management teams, business leaders, IT colleagues, and external partners. Success in the role requires strong collaboration across business, IT, OT, cybersecurity, and digital transformation teams to ensure technology creates measurable value for the business.
The position is preferably based at one of our operational smelter sites but can also be located at any of our other operational sites. Regular travel between sites will be required, along with occasional visits to other Boliden locations.

What you will do
As Head of IT Smelters, you will lead the technology agenda for Boliden's Smelter business and ensure that IT delivers measurable business value. Acting as a strategic partner to business leaders, you will define the long-term IT vision and roadmap, ensuring that technology supports both today's operational needs and the future development of the business. 
Key responsibilities include:
Define and execute the IT strategy, vision, and roadmap for the Smelter business. 
Partner with senior business leaders to align technology investments with business priorities and long-term objectives. 
Lead, develop, and inspire a team of seven IT managers and specialists. 
Drive digital transformation, innovation, and continuous improvement initiatives. 
Manage the IT portfolio, budget, and strategic technology investments. 
Ensure secure, reliable, and cost-effective IT services and solutions. 
Collaborate across Group IT and business functions to balance local needs with enterprise-wide priorities. 
Contribute to the broader IT leadership agenda and the long-term development of Boliden's technology landscape.

 
What you bring
You are a strategic and business-oriented IT leader with a passion for technology, transformation, and people leadership. You build strong relationships across the organization, drive change, and translate business needs into technology-enabled value.
Required qualifications:
Extensive experience in senior IT leadership roles, with a proven ability to lead leaders, build high-performing teams, and influence stakeholders in complex matrix organizations.
Strong track record of driving digital transformation and change. 
Proven ability to build trusted relationships with senior business leaders and translate business strategy into technology priorities.
Good understanding of IT governance, portfolio management, budgeting, and vendor management. 
Experience delivering secure and reliable IT services. 
Strong stakeholder management, communication, and influencing skills. 
University degree in Information Technology, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and practical experience.
Fluent in English, both written and spoken. Fluency in Swedish, Norwegian, or Finnish is considered an advantage.
A valid EU Category B driving licence, as the role involves regular travel to our sites

Meritorious qualifications:
Experience from industrial, manufacturing, mining, metals, energy, or other asset-intensive industries. 
Experience leading cross-functional teams and influencing stakeholders in a complex matrix organization. 
Knowledge of IT/OT integration and industrial digitalization. 
Experience with data & analytics, automation, AI, and emerging technologies. 
Knowledge of cybersecurity, cloud technologies, and enterprise architecture.

Why work with us
At Boliden, we believe in promoting a workplace where care, courage, and responsibility are central to everything we do. We offer a workplace where we believe in collaboration and where what you contribute will have a direct impact on future generations. We are a company made up of responsible and creative people all working towards the same vision; to become the most sustainable and respected metal supplier in the world.

Apply today to be part of something truly meaningful!
At Boliden, diversity and inclusion are drivers of innovation. We know that different perspectives and experiences strengthen us and help us stay at the forefront of an important and exciting industry. Therefore, we encourage applications from people with diverse backgrounds and viewpoints. Together, we build a workplace where everyone can feel safe and inspired to reach their full potential.
Want to know more about the position? Contact hiring manager, Mathias Nilsson, Mathias.Nilsson@boliden.com.
Questions about the application are answered by our Talent Acquisition Partner, Pernilla Åkerblom, Pernilla.Akerblom@boliden.com, +46 73-023 69 61.
For union information, please contact Mats Lindblom, SACO, +46 73-350 04 19, Andreas Mårtensson, Unionen, +46 70-541 83 93 or Peter Markström, Ledarna, +46 910-77 40 09. 
We welcome your application no later than December 3, 2026.
As part of Boliden’s qualitative recruitment efforts and systematic safety work, background checks may be included in the recruitment process.

jobs.occupation: Platform Product Manager at Husqvarna Group
jobs.description:
Do you want to run a platform as a product, with developers as your customers?

Our mission is to enable our DevOps teams to focus on building great applications by providing a shared internal developer platform, tools, templates and ways of working that simplify the entire software development lifecycle. Today, we support more than 20 teams across all three divisions, combining hands-on engineering with coaching, training and technical enablement.

Ultimately, our goal is simple: remove complexity, create great developer experiences and enable teams to deliver secure, high-quality software faster.

Role Description
CORE Platform gives our DevOps teams a paved road to build, test, deploy and observe software safely and efficiently. Our ambition is to create a platform that teams choose because it makes their work easier, not simply because they have to use it.

As Platform Product Manager, you will treat the platform as a product, with developers as your customers. You will stay close to our DevOps teams, understand their needs and use feedback and data to shape priorities, set goals and build a roadmap focused on outcomes rather than output.

Working closely with domain leads and platform engineers, you will help ensure CORE Platform feels like one coherent developer experience rather than a collection of tools. You will connect technical platform development with the wider needs of Husqvarna Group, helping us invest where we can create the greatest value for both developers and the business.

Looking ahead, we are also preparing for AI agents to become platform users alongside developers. You will help shape what this means for the platform and how it influences our future priorities. What you will do:

Shape the platform strategy and roadmap based on user needs, business priorities and measurable outcomes.
Work closely with developers to understand their needs, test ideas early and create effective feedback loops.
Translate developer and business needs into clear platform priorities.
Define and follow up on goals and metrics around adoption, developer experience and platform value.
Work with domain leads and platform engineers to create a consistent and coherent platform experience.

The final phase of a delivery is where our technology truly proves itself. Installation at the shipyard, commissioning, HAT and SAT, final acceptance, and the warranty period are critical stages in ensuring that the vessel performs as promised. They are also the moments that shape the customer’s lasting impression of our delivery.
To strengthen our focus on this critical phase, we are now establishing a new Commissioning & Warranty function and are looking for two individuals to join the team who want to help shape it from the start. In this role, you will take operational responsibility for the delivery through its most decisive stage, where engineering is transformed into real-world performance and customer value.
What you will be doing
As Responsible for Commissioning & Warranty, you are operationally responsible for a delivery from formal project handover, after FAT and delivery of the equipment, until the customer is transferred to standard Aftermarket support. You will plan, coordinate, and drive the delivery forward through arrival inspection, installation support, commissioning, HAT and SAT, customer acceptance, the warranty period, and ultimately formal warranty closure. Your mission is clear: keep everything moving until we leave behind vessels that perform as promised and customers who trust us to deliver again.
Throughout this journey, you will be the customer’s primary operational point of contact, providing continuity, direction, and clear ownership from one phase to the next. Internally, you will be the connecting force between our technical, operational, and supporting functions, bringing the right people together, aligning priorities, and ensuring that the delivery continues to move forward.
In practice, you will:
Take over the delivery from the Project Manager and make sure nothing falls between the two of you: scope, open points, documentation and warranty terms.
Coordinate field service resources and spare parts, and collaborate with Subject Matter Experts (SMEs), technical support and suppliers to secure competence and availability against plan;
Ensure arrival inspection at site is completed and drive transport damage and shortages to resolution.
Support installation towards the shipyard, then plan and run commissioning, HAT and SAT until acceptance is obtained.
Act as operational owner of warranty cases, from registration and technical assessment to liability determination and resolution, including claim handling and supplier recovery.
Handle customer disputes and negotiate practical, commercially sound settlements within your mandate.
Keep scope boundaries, documentation, cost exposure and status visible and feed lessons learned back into engineering, production and service.

You work within a clear mandate. Decisions on prioritization, technical resolution paths, resourcing, warranty assessment and settlements within your delegated authority are yours to make. The Project Manager remains accountable for the overall project, and the genuinely large questions are escalated but you are expected to solve, not to forward.
We think you should have
You have led projects before and know what it takes to keep stakeholders aligned when schedules are under pressure. You are comfortable being the main point of contact for customers and enjoy balancing technical, commercial and operational perspectives to move a project forward.
We believe you have several years of experience in project management, commissioning management, or aftermarket/service management, preferably within the marine, offshore, energy, or other capital equipment industries. You hold a technical degree or have gained equivalent knowledge through practical experience. You have worked closely with shipyards, customers and suppliers, handling deviations, claims and commercial discussions, and you possess a solid technical understanding that allows you to actively participate in discussions with engineers and service technicians, form your own view of technical challenges, and contribute to finding solutions.
You are comfortable working across multiple IT systems simultaneously, such as ERP platforms, case and claim management systems, documentation tools and reporting solutions. You also have a good understanding of contracts, warranty terms and the commercial impact of technical decisions. Fluency in English, both written and spoken, is required, while Swedish is considered an advantage. The role also involves occasional travel to shipyards, vessels and customer sites as needed, although travel is not the primary focus of the position.
Just as important as your experience is the way you work. You are structured and proactive, with a natural ability to bring tasks to completion rather than letting them drift. You remain calm and professional in challenging situations, focusing on finding solutions and building strong relationships. You communicate clearly with people from different cultures, backgrounds and levels of an organization, and you take ownership of your responsibilities without waiting to be directed.
Why join us
A role with real influence. Commissioning and warranty is where our promises to the customer are tested. We are building a clearer, more structured and more customer-focused way of working around it and you will help us shape it. Your work strengthens the transition between New Sales, Project Management and the Aftermarket organization, with better quality, stronger documentation, reduced cost leakage and stronger customer relationships as the result.
A global and technologically advanced environment. World-leading products for vessel propulsion, experienced colleagues and international customers. You will work closely with Project Management, Technical Support, Field Service, Engineering, our Product Centers and the regional Global Customer Support organizations, and build a cross-functional network across the business that few other roles give you.
Breadth, and room to grow. Few positions combine technology, coordination, customer dialogue, business understanding and continuous improvement the way this one does. It sits in a stable global organization with a strong culture of innovation, and offers good development opportunities in whichever direction you want to take next.
We offer flexible working hours and the option to work remote or from home office.

Security Clearance is required for this position.

TL;DR
You're a communications professional who can plan and execute the work that advances Lovable's objectives across EU and Swedish policy environments, making sure our voice is heard on the issues that matter most. You'll pair sharp corporate communications with real policy fluency — working closely with internal teams and external partners to help policymakers, media, and other stakeholders understand Lovable's perspective on the key files and issues that shape the environment we operate in.
This is a balanced role, equal parts policy operator and corporate communicator. You'll report to the European Communications and Public Affairs Lead.
Why Lovable?
Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.
We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.
Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.
What you'll do
This role makes sure Lovable has a credible, constructive voice in the rooms that matter — building a presence worth listening to and developing clear positions that reflect what Lovable actually builds and believes.
Advocate Lovable's positions on key policy files. You'll build and run our engagement with policy representatives across EU and Swedish institutions.
Own corporate communications on policy issues. Statements, briefings, op-eds, speaking moments, and the proactive announcements that build credibility over time. You'll develop the strategy, write the materials, manage media relationships, and make sure each piece reinforces the others.
Track the regulatory agenda and turn it into a point of view. You'll monitor the files that affect us and develop clear positions that reflect the company's reality and ambitions.
Build coalitions and work through industry. You'll represent Lovable in trade associations and industry groups, finding shared causes that move issues forward.
Act as a comms and policy partner to our cross-functional team. You'll work closely with the communications and cross-functional teams in preparing for engagements with policymakers, institutions, and press, strengthening the company’s voice in the European AI debate.
Who you are
You've operated in and around the policy world. That might mean an EU institution, a trade association, a think tank, or a public affairs firm. Wherever you've been, you know how a file moves from idea to law, and you can read the politics, formal and informal, that determine what actually happens.
You understand policy and can communicate it. You have experience from both policy work and corporate communications, and you're equally comfortable speaking to policymakers and media alike.
You can drive an issue forward in a complex political environment. You're comfortable with ambiguity and competing agendas, and you know how to prioritize when everything feels urgent.
You're a sharp writer with editorial judgment. You can turn a dense regulatory development into a crisp briefing, opinion piece or clean position statement.
You connect dots that other people don't see. You look at a piece of draft legislation and think ahead on what it means for the industry as well as what Lovable should say and to whom.
You're a genuine cross-functional collaborator. You work easily with cross-functional stakeholders, external partners, and coalitions. You don't wait to be invited into the room. You're not precious about who gets credit. You just make things work.
You're deeply curious about AI, technology policy, and the industry landscape. You keep up with what happens in the world instinctively — the news, the regulatory moves, the debates as they unfold. You understand where the conversation is heading well enough to spot a risk or an opportunity before someone hands it to you.
What you need to know
This is not a role where you set the strategy and hand off execution. You'll be writing the first drafts of our position statements, building the relationships and showing up in the room as a Lovable representative.
We move fast and plans change. The job runs on two clocks at once: you'll react to the urgent issue that lands today while building the relationships and positions that set us up for success in the long term. If you need a settled environment with predictable workflows, this will be frustrating. If you find that kind of pace energizing, you'll love it.
We're building public affairs and communications at a company that is itself being built. That means you'll have real influence over how this function develops in Europe: the positions, the relationships, the standards. That's the upside of being early.
Finally: joining Lovable Comms means you're deeply curious, data-driven, and not extremely precious about role boundaries. You find ways to work smarter with AI, to measure what matters, and to step into work that isn't technically "yours" when the moment calls for it.
About your application
Please submit your application in English. It’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join.
We treat all candidates equally - if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal.

This is an opportunity to help shape both a product and the way of working around it. You will build and lead a small, high-trust development team where AI accelerates engineering without compromising quality, security or maintainability.
About the role
As Engineering Manager for HiveAI, you lead the people and shape how the team works and delivers. You will lead an international team with developers based across several Fellowmind countries, so building trust, alignment and a strong team culture across locations will be an important part of your leadership.
You will work as a peer alongside our Product Manager and Chief Architect, each with a clear but closely connected area of ownership. The Product Manager drives the why and what. The way we build matters. The HiveAI team works from problems and hypotheses, using AI to move quickly from idea to experiment and prototype. What proves valuable is then hardened into secure, scalable and maintainable software. You will help define what this way of working looks like in practice as the team grows.
You will lead a team that brings together platform developers, who build and maintain HiveAI itself, and Frontier Fellows (Forward Deployed Engineers), who work close to our implementation teams and customers and bring what they learn and build back into the product. What you will do:
Build and lead the team. Own hiring, 1:1s, development and performance conversations, and build a strong, high-trust engineering culture across a distributed international team.
Design the way we deliver. Drive fast build-and-learn cycles, remove impediments and favour working demos and clear ship, change or stop decisions.
Turn prototypes into products. Together with the Chief Architect, make sure promising experiments cross the line into production with the engineering quality they need.
Make AI a real engineering capability. Coach developers in prompting, coding agents, AI-assisted testing and code review, and continuously evolve how the team works with AI.

You probably spent a significant part of your career as a software developer before moving into technical and people leadership. Today, you might be an Engineering Manager, Software Development Manager or a Tech Lead with people responsibility, ideally in a SaaS or software product company.
You are comfortable when the destination is clearer than the route to get there. You coach and enable your team, make good decisions with incomplete information and know when a fast prototype is good enough to learn from, but not good enough to ship.
We believe that you bring:
Extensive professional experience in software development, followed by at least 2–3 years of people leadership, either as an Engineering Manager or as a Tech Lead with direct people responsibility.
Hands-on experience using AI coding tools and agents, such as GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code or similar, as part of real software development.
Strong engineering practices across CI/CD, automated testing, code review and secure development.
Experience from a SaaS or software product environment, where teams own what they build beyond the first release.
Experience leading distributed or international teams, with the ability to coach, communicate and build a strong team culture across locations, mainly through digital ways of working.
